title: Published key insertion sort: exact byte order
security_scope: Adapted port of insertion_sort_by_keys only, with an explicit strict two-tree-argument module wrapper. The first input is not presorted or fully validated. Empty insertions return any sorted tree unchanged; an empty sorted tree can accept a malformed single entry without reading its key. Comparisons require atom keys and use unsigned lexicographic byte order, preserving padding, arbitrary payloads and any unvisited improper tail. Equal-key placement is stable when the initial list is descending; no stability guarantee is added for unsorted input. Nonempty zero atoms are not nil. Malformed paths reject only when visited. This is finite helper evidence, not verification of the enclosing credential proof checker, a protocol, a canonical module hash, authorization, constant-time behavior or compiler preservation.

source_span.extraction: Exact upstream source lines, including indentation and trailing LF; this extracted span is not a tracked upstream file.

source_adaptation.description: Embed both exact upstream spans in a self-contained module. Add only a proper two-argument outer environment check; pass both arbitrary trees to the original helper. No key, list or tail validation is added to the helper.

limitations: Only insertion_sort_by_keys and its required or macro are adapted; the enclosing credential proof checker, merge sort and repository are not ported.
This visible module adapter is new; no identity with the published whole puzzle or curried instance is claimed.
The helper assumes its first list is sorted but does not enforce or repair that assumption; malformed entries and tails can remain unvisited and accepted.
Whole-input/output/work limits belong to the native oracle and VM harness, not the public policy. Resource and infrastructure errors are inconclusive, never policy rejection.
Finite comparisons and an independent data oracle do not prove compiler preservation, universal resource bounds, authorization or constant-time behavior.
